leads.title: Niger Charte de la Refondation (Refoundation Charter), Article 25
leads.documents: Criminalization of all LGBTQIA+ acts/practices (pratiques); basis for 2025 explicit outlawing of same-sex sexual activity
leads.detail: Cited as Article 25, adopted March 2025 by ruling military junta; no URL visible in text

leads.title: Niger New Penal Code (February 2026, marriage provisions June 2026)
leads.documents: Sanctions 5-10 years prison + fine up to 100M CFA for same-sex relations, public announcement of same-sex relationship, and changing or attempting to change one's birth sex; 10-20 years + fine up to 500M CFA for creating/managing/financing/participating in LGBTQIA+ organizations/clubs/venues; no mitigating circumstances or suspended sentences
leads.detail: Cited as new penal code adopted February 2026, marriage sanctions effective June 2026; no URL visible in text

leads.title: Niger Charte de la Refondation, Article 24
leads.documents: Legal definition of marriage as union between a man and a woman; basis for non-recognition of same-sex unions
leads.detail: Cited as Article 24, in force since March 2025; no URL visible in text

leads.title: Statement by Minister of Justice and Human Rights Alio Daouda
leads.documents: Government intent/policy that all LGBTQ practices are not in line with social and cultural values, supporting criminal code measures
leads.detail: Quoted as: all LGBTQ practices, whatever they may be (...) are not in line with our social and cultural values; no outlet/URL visible

leads.title: Law 2022-59 on Protection of Personal Data, Article 95
leads.documents: Limited protection: punishes collecting/processing data revealing sexual life or sexual orientation with 3 months-5 years + 5M-50M CFA fine
leads.detail: Cited as Article 95, exceptions in Article 42; published June 2025 by Ministry of Communication and New Information Technologies (MCNTI); no URL visible

leads.title: Law 2015-36 on Illicit Trafficking of Migrants, Art. 4 + 2023 repeal decree
leads.documents: Former non-discrimination protection including sexual orientation, then repealed; shows removal of rights machinery
leads.detail: Cited as repealed in 2023 by decree of President Abdourahamane Tiani; government stated convictions expunged and law criminalized lawful activities; no URL visible

leads.title: U.S. Department of State 2013 Human Rights Report on Niger
leads.documents: Societal discrimination, pressure to conform, secret gay rights organizations, enforcement example of two men arrested for public indecency in parked car and fined; no reported violence/discrimination in employment/housing/education/healthcare, likely underreported
leads.detail: Cited as 2013 Human Rights Report; no URL visible in text

leads.title: 2022 Niamey LGBTQ asylum-seeker protest at Office of High Commissioner for Refugees
leads.documents: Living conditions and rights machinery: first public LGBTQ demonstration by asylum seekers from Cameroon, Liberia, Cote d'Ivoire; denial of refugee status hindering relocation; societal discrimination and verbal/physical violence
leads.detail: Cited as 2022 protest in Niamey in front of UNHCR office plus local correspondent account; no outlet/URL visible

leads.title: 2022 Maradi prosecution and parliamentary proposal by lawmaker Nana Djibou Harouna
leads.documents: Enforcement attempt: two young women prosecuted for lesbianism, acquitted for lack of legislation but imprisoned 2 years for nude videos allegedly portraying lesbian act; subsequent proposal to outlaw same-sex relationships
leads.detail: Cited as Maradi 2022 case and Harouna proposal to Parliament; also 2023 President Mohamed Bazoum proposal for anti-LGBTQ Penal Code adaptation; no URL visible

leads.title: 2025 Niamey public indecency acquittal and 2026 local media mass-arrest reports
leads.documents: Enforcement under Charter and Penal Code: 2025 prosecution of two women reported as lesbians acquitted as not public sphere, judge allegedly sanctioned for leniency and public debate; 2026 reports of dozens arrested including military officials, LGBTQ people in hiding, HIV prevention services to MSM stopped (condoms/testing/PrEP loss)
leads.detail: Cited as 2025 Niamey case and 2026 local media reports; no outlet names/URLs visible in text
